title: Faster mixing near a surface
hook: Change heat-transfer coefficient and predict convective heat rate.
misconception: convective heat rate stays fixed when heat-transfer coefficient doubles.
objective: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT to compare convective heat rate when heat-transfer coefficient changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With fixed surface area and surface-to-fluid temperature difference, Q̇ = hAΔT. When heat-transfer coefficient doubles, convective heat rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = hAΔT; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider fixed surface area and surface-to-fluid temperature difference, with a nonzero initial result. If heat-transfer coefficient triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on convective heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
